purpose: Keep synthetic browser samples and their provenance for reproducible comparisons; neither record is a verified historical best.
limitations: The 200 ms wait is included in completion timing and is not measured work; frame timing is affected by frame phase.
The V8 sampled retained heap is an estimate and is not total allocation.
Both records contain seven measurements from a single browser process, not multi-process alternating confirmation.
The older raw file did not record browser version, hardware, fonts, complete resource identity, or a capture time; do not assume that its environment matches the later record.
The original local benchmark script was subsequently modified. The tracked fixture reconstructs its last recorded scenario, but the original script hash is not available.
The preliminary working-tree record preceded the change from per-turn linear search to a map while building the bookmark index; its menu-opening measurements do not identify the final implementation.

The two original local-script records loaded the old index from Git but loaded external JavaScript and vendor assets from the current worktree. The tracked runner instead reads the entire old prototype from one commit, so its method differs from those archived measurements.
A compact historical best may only be promoted after comparable environments and repeated alternating measurements have been verified.
